I have read the full file. Now I have a complete picture of the current implementation. Let me design the fix plan. Here is the complete implementation plan for eliminating the CLS on the "My Jobs" table. --- ## Analysis of the Current Layout Shift **Root cause 1 - Column widths:** The `` has no ``, so the browser infers column widths from cell content. Skeleton cells all have `w-full` inside uniform `px-4 py-3.5` padding, which spreads weight evenly across 7 columns. When real data arrives the browser re-lays out to reflect the actual content (narrow checkbox, wide job title, narrow number, 44px circle, badge, date text, tiny icon), causing a full column-width reflow. **Root cause 2 - Pagination footer:** `!loading && filtered.length > 0` on line 635 means the footer does not exist in the DOM during loading. Its height (~48px with padding `py-3`) suddenly appears after data resolves, causing a height jump at the bottom of the card. **Root cause 3 - SkeletonRow padding mismatch:** Col 1 (checkbox) uses `pl-5 pr-2` on real rows but the skeleton uses `px-4` everywhere. Even with a colgroup the first cell will paint differently wide in skeleton vs loaded state if the padding differs. --- ## Fix 1 - Add a `` with fixed/percentage widths A `` is the only reliable way to lock column widths independent of cell content in an HTML table. The browser honours `` widths before it ever measures content, so both skeleton rows and real data rows share the same column geometry. **Proposed column widths** (total = 100%, table width = full container): | Col | Content | Proposed width | |-----|---------|----------------| | 1 | Checkbox | `40px` fixed | | 2 | Job Title | `auto` (absorbs remaining space) | | 3 | Resumes | `80px` fixed | | 4 | Avg Match Score | `120px` fixed | | 5 | Status | `110px` fixed | | 6 | Created On | `110px` fixed | | 7 | Arrow | `48px` fixed | Using pixel values for the narrow columns and no explicit width (or `w-auto`) for the Job Title column lets the title column flex while the rest are pinned. The `
` must also get `table-layout: fixed` so the browser respects `` widths without measuring content. Add class `table-fixed` (Tailwind) to the `
` element. **Exact insertion point** - immediately after `
` on line 508, before ``: ```tsx
{/* 40px — checkbox */} {/* auto — job title (flex) */} {/* 80px — resumes */} {/* 120px — avg score */} {/* 110px — status */} {/* 110px — created on */} {/* 48px — arrow */} ... ``` Note: `w-10` = 40px and `w-12` = 48px in Tailwind's default scale. `w-20` = 80px. The arbitrary `w-[120px]` and `w-[110px]` values are required because there are no exact Tailwind preset equivalents. --- ## Fix 2 - Update `SkeletonRow` to match real row structure Replace the current uniform `SkeletonRow` with one that mirrors each column's actual padding and uses a skeleton width representative of that column's content. This eliminates the padding-induced micro-reflow even if a colgroup is already locking overall widths. **Current (lines 173-181):** ```tsx const SkeletonRow = () => ( {[1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7].map((i) => ( ))} ); ``` **Replacement:** ```tsx const SkeletonRow = () => ( {/* Col 1: Checkbox — matches pl-5 pr-2 py-3.5, 16px square skeleton */} {/* Col 2: Job Title — matches px-4 py-3.5, icon + text line */} {/* Col 3: Resumes — matches px-4 py-3.5, short number */} {/* Col 4: Avg Match Score — matches px-4 py-3.5, 44px circle */} {/* Col 5: Status — matches px-4 py-3.5, badge shape */} {/* Col 6: Created On — matches px-4 py-3.5, date text width */} {/* Col 7: Arrow — matches px-4 py-3.5, small icon */} ); ``` Key decisions: - Col 1 uses `pl-5 pr-2` (not `px-4`) to match the actual checkbox cell padding on line 567. - Col 2 shows both the icon skeleton (rounded-lg, 36px square = `h-9 w-9`) and two text line skeletons stacked, mirroring the real cell's flex layout. - Col 4 uses `rounded-full` to suggest the circular score ring. - Col 5 uses `rounded-full` to suggest the badge pill shape. - Widths are intentionally narrow (not `w-full`) so they do not fight the colgroup on narrow containers. --- ## Fix 3 - Skeleton pagination footer during loading The pagination footer is currently conditional on `!loading && filtered.length > 0` (line 635). During loading, this entire block is absent from the DOM — the card is shorter by the footer height (~48px on desktop), which causes a vertical jump when loading resolves. The fix is to always render a footer-height placeholder when loading is true, then swap to the real footer when data arrives. **Replace lines 634-688:** ```tsx {/* ── Pagination ── */} {loading ? ( /* Skeleton footer — same height as real footer to prevent height jump */
) : filtered.length > 0 ? (

Showing {startIndex}–{endIndex} of {filtered.length} job{filtered.length !== 1 ? "s" : ""}

{totalPages > 1 && (
{Array.from({ length: totalPages }).map((_, i) => { const pageNum = i + 1; const nearCurrent = Math.abs(pageNum - page) <= 1; const isFirst = pageNum === 1; const isLast = pageNum === totalPages; if (!nearCurrent && !isFirst && !isLast) { if (pageNum === 2 && page > 3) return …; if (pageNum === totalPages - 1 && page < totalPages - 2) return …; return null; } return ( ); })}
)}
) : null} ``` The skeleton footer renders `py-3` + `border-t` matching the real footer exactly. It shows a count text skeleton on the left and four pagination button skeletons on the right (Prev, two page numbers, Next) to approximate the common case. When there is only one page of results `totalPages === 1`, the real footer shows no pagination buttons — but the skeleton always shows them. This is acceptable because the skeleton represents the loading state before we know the page count, and the total height difference from button row vs no button row is negligible compared to the jump from no-footer to footer. --- ## Fix 4 - Confirm filter bar is always visible Lines 441-483 are inside `` but outside any `{loading ? ... : ...}` conditional. The filter bar renders unconditionally regardless of loading state. No change is needed here — this is already correct. --- ## Summary of all changes to `JobsOverviewCard.tsx` **Change 1 — Line 508** (`
` opening tag): - Before: `

` - Add `` block with 7 `` elements immediately after. **Change 2 — Lines 173-181** (`SkeletonRow`): - Replace the 7-cell loop with 7 individually structured cells matching per-column padding and skeleton dimensions. **Change 3 — Lines 635-688** (pagination footer): - Wrap in `loading ? : filtered.length > 0 ? : null` ternary. No changes are needed to the filter bar (Fix 4 confirmed). --- ## Potential implementation pitfalls 1. **`table-fixed` and auto column:** With `table-layout: fixed`, the browser sizes columns strictly from the ``. The Job Title `` has no explicit width so it receives all remaining space after fixed columns are allocated. Verify that `40 + 80 + 120 + 110 + 110 + 48 = 508px` leaves enough space for the Job Title column on the smallest expected viewport (likely ~768px). At 768px the title column gets ~260px, which comfortably accommodates the `max-w-[220px]` truncated text plus the 36px icon and 12px gap. 2. **Colgroup Tailwind classes on ``:** Tailwind's JIT scanner will tree-shake `w-[120px]` and `w-[110px]` on `` elements only if it sees them in source. Since these are JSX literals in `.tsx`, the scanner will find them. No `safelist` change is needed. 3. **Skeleton footer height parity:** The skeleton footer uses `py-3` (12px top + 12px bottom = 24px padding) plus content height. The real footer also uses `py-3`. Both have `border-t`. The heights will be identical as long as skeleton content height equals real text/button height. The `h-3.5` text skeleton (14px) matches the real `text-xs` line height. The `h-7` button skeletons (28px) match the real `h-7` buttons. Heights are aligned. 4. **`last:border-0` on skeleton rows:** The current `SkeletonRow` has `last:border-0`, which is preserved. The 5 skeleton rows will have the last one without a bottom border, matching the real row behavior. --- ### Critical Files for Implementation - `/Users/yashbaldha/Desktop/Boldteq App/Rankora/src/components/JobsOverviewCard.tsx`
